implicit learning is context dependent, and that consolidation is a function of both the duration of initial training (satiation) and of time (time-dependent consolidation).
implicit visuomotor adaptation is subject to different types of interference and that the consolidation process is sensitive to initial training.

the neural basis of procedural learning and memory and the mechanisms by which the brain learns and stores new information.
the nature of implicit motor learning and the factors that affect the consolidation of motor memories.
the mechanisms and principles of motor learning and memory.

the study of visuomotion rotation has provided a rich source of findings and principles of general relevance to procedural learning, memory, and consolidation.
rotation learning is a model of motor learning that has many features that are common to procedural learning and motor memory.
motor learning is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
motor memory for a rotation learning task is subject to a number of different forms of interference and consolidation.
implicit motor memory is subject to a number of principles that are likely to be of general importance to motor and cognitive memory.
motor learning and memory are characterized by the interaction of implicit and explicit processes and that consolidation occurs through a number of different mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
implicit motor memory is not just about motor learning but also about motor memory consolidation.
motor learning is a dynamic process, which is subject to a variety of forms of learning and memory interference, and which consolidates over time.

the principles governing rotation learning are not specific to the particular visuomotor task used in the laboratory, but rather are likely general principles that apply to other forms of motor learning.
